title: They were chosen by God…
paragraphs:
They were chosen by God…
—but still losing battles in secret.
Read that again.

Chosen.
Anointed.
Used.
And yet… breaking inside.
That’s the detail most people miss.

We celebrate the victories.
The miracles.
The moments God moved through them.
But we ignore the fractures beneath the surface.

The fear in Gideon’s chest.
The pride creeping into Samson’s strength.
The silent compromises of David’s heart.
The hesitation in Moses’ voice when God called him.
And if we’re honest…
That story sounds a little too familiar.

Because you can be showing up in public—
serving, leading, posting, smiling—
while privately battling things no one else sees.

Secret sin.
Quiet shame.
Hidden cycles you swore you’d already broken.
You love God.
But there are rooms in your heart you still won’t let Him enter.
And here’s the tension:
God can use you… even while something in you is still undone.
But that is not the goal.
That is mercy.
Not maturity.
Not freedom.
Not transformation.
Look at what Scripture reveals:
“Now the Spirit of the Lord came upon Gideon…” — Judges 6:34
Yet just chapters later, Gideon builds an ephod that leads Israel into idolatry (Judges 8:27).
“Then the Spirit of the Lord rushed upon Samson…” — Judges 14:6
Yet Samson’s life was marked by impulsive desire and moral compromise (Judges 16).
“The Lord is my shepherd…” — Psalm 23:1

David could write worship that still shakes the earth—
yet he also fell into adultery and orchestrated death (2 Samuel 11).
Feel the weight of that.

God’s power can rest on a person…
while their private life is still at war.
Some scholars interpret these moments as evidence of God’s covenant faithfulness despite human failure. Others emphasize them as warnings—showing that gifting is never a substitute for godliness.
Either way, the message is clear:
Anointing is not the same as surrender.
And that should shake you—in the best way.
Because maybe you’ve been measuring your spiritual health by what God does through you…
instead of what God is doing in you.

Miracles don’t always mean maturity.
Platform doesn’t always mean purity.
Impact doesn’t always mean intimacy with God.
Let that sink in.

You can cast out demons…
and still be bound in secret.

You can lead others…
and still be lost in certain areas.
That’s why Jesus said:
“Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven…” — Matthew 7:21–23
That verse is not meant to scare you away.
It’s meant to wake you up.
Because God never intended to just use you.
He wants to transform you.

Deeply.
Fully.
Honestly.
And this is where everything shifts.
Because the story of imperfect deliverers is not pointing to them.
It’s pointing to the One they could never be.
Jesus Christ.
The only Deliverer with no cracks.

No compromise.
No hidden sin.
No divided heart.

Where others were empowered temporarily,
Jesus is righteous eternally.

Where others saved for a moment,
Jesus saves forever.
“For we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but one who in every respect has been tempted as we are, yet without sin.” — Hebrews 4:15
Let that hit your heart.

He understands your struggle—
but He is not trapped by it.
And because of that…
He can actually set you free.

Not manage your sin.
Not hide your shame.
Destroy it.
This is the Gospel:
You are not just flawed.
You are a sinner in need of rescue.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
But God did not leave you there.

Jesus stepped into your mess—
lived the life you couldn’t live—
died the death you deserved—
and rose again so you could be made new.
“But God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
This is not behavior modification.
This is resurrection.
You don’t need better discipline first.
You need surrender.
Real surrender.

Not partial obedience.
Not selective repentance.
Everything.
Because here’s the truth most people avoid:

God is not impressed with your performance
if your heart is still divided.
He doesn’t just want your gift.
He wants you.
All of you.

The parts you show…
and the parts you hide.
So let me ask you—
What are you still keeping from Him?

That habit?
That mindset?
That relationship?
That secret no one knows?
Bring it into the light.
Not tomorrow.
Now.
“If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” — 1 John 1:9
Cleanse.
Not cover.
Not ignore.
Cleanse.
You don’t have to live split anymore.

Public strength.
Private struggle.
That’s not freedom.
Jesus didn’t die so you could manage sin.
He died so you could be free from it.
Completely.
This is your moment.
Not to feel condemned.
But to come home.

Drop the mask.
Lay down the weight.
Stop performing.
Start surrendering.
Say it plainly:
“Jesus, I give You everything.”
Not just your strengths.
Your secrets too.
And watch what happens when grace meets honesty.
Freedom.
Real freedom.
If this hit you where it hurts… where it’s real…
And if this stirred something deep in you…
